steps.message:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-15, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1132.2 | 7.42 | 7.42
2 | 3621.5 | 17.67 | 25.09
3 | 4447.9 | 1.70 | 26.79
4 | 4307.5 | 0.53 | 27.32
5 | 7664.9 | 4.92 | 32.24
6 | 12762.9 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as HKHA-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-15, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report — Station T-15, Survey Area T**

The VES interpretation yields a 6-layer model with resistivities increasing overall from 1132.2 Ω·m at surface to 12762.9 Ω·m at depth, with a thin low-resistivity layer (4307.5 Ω·m) sandwiched between two higher-resistivity layers (4447.9 and 7664.9 Ω·m) at 26.79–27.32 m depth. Layer thicknesses range from 0.53 m to 17.67 m, with the last layer unbounded.

Applying the curve-type rule to resistivities 1132.2, 3621.5, 4447.9, 4307.5, 7664.9, 12762.9 gives triplet codes A (r1<r2<r3), K (r2<r3, r3>r4), H (r3>r4<r5), A (r4<r5<r6), yielding **AKHA**, not the filed **HKHA**. The discrepancy appears in the first letter (A vs. H). Recommend verifying the layer resistivity values against the raw sounding data before finalizing the classification.
